title: Syntactic retry DSL and AsyncStream ViewBridge (typed stream handles + auth decorator)
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: developers building multi-step streaming integrations repeatedly implement small retry wrappers and ad-hoc stream adapters to reconcile push vs pull models and credential rotations. This PR introduces two ergonomic primitives: (1) a small declarative/syntactic retry DSL (RetrySpec) that compiles to runtime retry policies (backoff, idempotency predicate, max attempts, jitter) and (2) AsyncStream ViewBridge: a lightweight typed adapter that exposes the same async-iterator interface while allowing push-based transports and credential-swap decorators to interoperate. Design goals: make the default ergonomics pleasant for TypeScript consumers, keep the runtime dependency-free, and make the spec serializable so CLI tools and config layers can emit retry bundles. Checklist: - [x] RetrySpec type and compiler -> runtime hooks - [x] retry decorator: @withRetry(fn, spec) and functional withRetry(fn, spec) - [x] AsyncStream.ViewBridge class with attach/detach semantics - [x] typed StreamHandle export for first-class consumer control (pause/resume/peek) - [x] Small auth decorator compatible with credential chains (supports sync and async refresh) - [x] Cross-SDK API notes for Python/Go (docs change stubbed) - [x] Tests: unit + integration with mock server - [x] CI: lint, build, unit, integration passing What changed (high level commits): 1) introduce RetrySpec types, parser and default presets 2) export withRetry decorator and functional helper with compact ergonomics 3) implement AsyncStream.ViewBridge and StreamHandle primitives 4) add CredentialDecorator that composes with withRetry for token refresh + idempotent hints 5) tests and small example consumer in examples/streaming/retry-viewbridge.ts Backwards compatibility: this is additive. The decorator and ViewBridge are opt-in APIs; existing push/pull adapters remain untouched. Example usage (consumer): const spec = RetrySpec.from({backoff: 'exp', baseMs: 100, maxAttempts: 4, idempotent: (err) => err.code !== '400'}); const decorated = withRetry(async () => { const stream = new AsyncStream.ViewBridge(transport); const handle = stream.open(); for await (const chunk of handle) { process(chunk); } }, spec); The CredentialDecorator can be composed: const secured = CredentialDecorator.wrap(decorated, {refresh: async () => fetchNewToken()}); Migration notes: - Add small opt-in import: import {withRetry, RetrySpec, AsyncStream, CredentialDecorator} from '@redwood/sdk'; - No behavior change if consumers don't adopt new imports; feature targeted at high-throughput streaming integrations and connector implementers.
commit_summary: feat(retry): add RetrySpec DSL and compiler; feat(stream): AsyncStream.ViewBridge and StreamHandle; feat(auth): CredentialDecorator composable with withRetry; test: unit + integration for retry/stream combos; docs: usage example

Luca Romano: Nice ergonomics, I like the RetrySpec shape. Please ensure we don't pull in any runtime polyfills.
Maya Patel: Agree, design avoids new deps; compiler emits plain JS. Added a small shim in tests for Node < 18.

Daniel Ortega: The ViewBridge pause/resume semantics look racy with underlying transport 'drain' event. Need safer shutdown handling.
Maya Patel: Addressed by deferring close until drain resolved and added tests for in-flight messages during shutdown.

release_notes:
- New RetrySpec DSL and withRetry decorator for compact declarative retries
- AsyncStream.ViewBridge and typed StreamHandle for safe push/pull interop
- CredentialDecorator to compose token refresh with retry policies
- Backwards-compatible, opt-in APIs
